Senior C++ Software Engineer

Remote (UK-based) | Full-Time

About Us

Reactive Markets is the 2026 OTC Trading Platform of the Year (Risk.net). Our network handles over $75 billion in daily trading volumes across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency, connecting 50+ of the world's leading liquidity providers.

We build trading systems that operate at the edge of what's technically possible — where nanoseconds matter and a dropped message costs real money. Our engineering team is small, senior, and deeply invested in the craft of building cutting edge, reliable, high-performance systems.

The Role

We're looking for a Senior C++ Software Engineer who can shape the technical direction of our Switchboard trading platform while continuing to write excellent code. You'll work on the most performance-critical components — pricing engines, connectivity gateways, market-data systems, and the messaging layer that ties them together — and you'll have a direct influence on architectural decisions that affect the entire platform.

This is not a role where you write code and throw it over a wall. You build it, you test it, you deploy it, you support it in production, and you improve it. Our engineers own the full lifecycle — from design through to operational excellence. When something breaks at 4pm on a Friday, you're part of the team that investigates and fixes it.

Beyond your own delivery, you'll provide technical oversight across the team — reviewing designs, challenging assumptions, and mentoring engineers who are earlier in their careers. You'll help us maintain the quality bar that our clients depend on, and you'll contribute to the architectural decisions that determine how well our platform scales.

Occasional hours outside the normal working day are required for production releases, scheduled maintenance windows, and Level 3 support during critical incidents. We keep this to a minimum and recognise the commitment — but owning a production trading platform means being there when it matters.

What You'll Work On

  • Modern C++20 and Go on Linux — a modern software stack based on open source

  • Cloud-native infrastructure on AWS with colocation in key data centres

  • Microsecond-level latency optimisation and high-throughput messaging

  • Market-data and reference-data pipelines across multiple asset classes

  • FIX protocol integrations with global banks and liquidity providers

  • Observability and monitoring — dashboards, alerting, and metrics that make system behaviour visible

  • Production systems that handle real money — reliability is not optional

  • Architectural oversight — solution design, peer reviews, and technical direction for platform components

  • Mentorship — helping junior and mid-level engineers develop their skills, improve their code, and grow into stronger contributors

What We Need

Technical:

  • Strong C++ with Linux systems programming (5+ years)

  • Comfortable working close to the metal — you understand what's underneath your code

  • Proven track record of optimising complex, latency-sensitive systems — you can profile, diagnose, and fix performance problems methodically

  • Deep understanding of distributed systems architecture and network protocols (TCP/UDP, socket programming, FIX)

  • Experience with system design and architectural trade-offs — you've made decisions that stuck and lived with the consequences

  • Go experience is a strong bonus — we use Go extensively for microservices and command-line tooling, and you'll be expected to work with it internally. If you don't know it yet, strong C++ engineers pick it up quickly

  • Python for scripting, automation, testing, and data analysis — used across the platform for tooling and operational workflows

  • Git and shell scripting

  • Experience in financial services or trading technology is a plus but not essential

How you work:

  • You ship. You're delivery-focused — you iterate, you improve, you get things into production

  • You own it. When you build something, you take responsibility for its behaviour in production. You respond to incidents (15-minute acknowledgement SLA during working hours), investigate issues, and close the loop

  • You raise the bar. You conduct thoughtful peer reviews, challenge designs constructively, and hold the team to high standards without slowing it down

  • You mentor. You invest in the engineers around you — sharing knowledge, pairing on hard problems, and helping people grow. You make the team better, not just the code

  • You write things down. Documentation is not an afterthought — it's how we scale knowledge across a distributed team. If it's not written down, it doesn't exist

  • You communicate. We're a distributed team across multiple time zones. Clear, proactive communication — especially when things go wrong — is essential

  • You care about quality. You write clean, testable code. You review your peers' work thoughtfully. You push for continuous improvement without gold-plating

  • You embrace AI tooling. We use AI tools (Claude, Gemini) to amplify our engineering capability — from code review and debugging to incident investigation and documentation. You don't need to be an expert, but you should be curious and willing to learn

What You Get

  • Real problems — trading systems where performance is measured in microseconds, not user clicks

  • Technical influence — direct input into architectural decisions, solution design, and the technical direction of the platform

  • An excellent team — senior engineers who care about craft, collaborate openly, and hold each other to high standards

  • Ownership — small teams, clear accountability, direct impact on the platform and our clients

  • Competitive package — up to 30 days leave + bank holidays, private health insurance, pension, life insurance, dental/optical cashback, cycle to work, socials and offsites

  • Remote-friendly — work from home with flexibility. We trust our people to deliver

  • Sustainable pace — we work hard, but we don't burn people out. Balance is how we stay sharp

  • Growth — career progression to lead roles, performance specialisation, or technical leadership. We invest in people who invest in us

We believe in transparency, honest feedback, and writing things down. We celebrate delivery, not activity. We frame AI as empowering people — removing toil, amplifying capability, enabling higher-value work.

We aim to build systems that don't depend on the heroics of individuals to maintain and support — systems and processes that are resilient, documented, and sustainable.

Our Hiring Process

We keep our process focused and respectful of your time. Our process follows three stages.

Stage 1: Initial Conversation with Talent Acquisition
Format: Video call, ~30-45 minutes

Stage 2: Hiring Manager Conversation with the relevant team lead or hiring manager
Format: Video call, ~60 minutes

Stage 3: Technical Interview with two members of the relevant engineering team
Format: Video call, interactive session, ~60 minutes

What to expect in each stage will be explained by Talent Acquisition if you're invited to interview. Throughout the process, we aim to keep momentum with no unnecessary delays between stages, and feedback typically comes within a few business days.

*Please note that depending on availability, Stage 2 and 3 may swap around.

How to Apply

Please apply directly via this job posting — all applications, including those submitted via LinkedIn, are managed through our applicant tracking system, so you'll always land in the same place regardless of where you found this role.

 

Right to Work: Candidates must have the existing right to work in the UK. We are not currently able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Equal Opportunities: Reactive Markets is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation.

Reasonable Adjustments: If you need any adjustments or support during the application or interview process, please let us know — we're happy to accommodate.

Data Protection: By applying, you consent to Reactive Markets processing your personal data for recruitment purposes, in line with our privacy policy.

FIX Onboarding & Client Services, EMEA

Hybrid, London, UK (3+ days per week in-office) | Full-Time

About Us

Reactive Markets is the 2026 OTC Trading Platform of the Year (Risk.net). Our network handles over $75 billion in daily trading volumes across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency, connecting 50+ of the world's leading liquidity providers.

We build trading systems that operate at the edge of what's technically possible — where nanoseconds matter and a dropped message costs real money. Our engineering team is small, senior, and deeply invested in the craft of building cutting edge, reliable, high-performance systems.

The Role

We are seeking a motivated and technically curious Onboarding and Client Services professional to join our London team. This role will focus on FIX client onboarding, integrations, and client service delivery across FX, equities and digital assets. The successful candidate will work closely with clients and internal teams to ensure seamless connectivity, smooth integration, and exceptional service throughout the client lifecycle.

We're building genuinely AI-enabled tooling to support this function — so this role is less about arriving with a decade of FIX expertise already committed to memory, and much more about someone sharp, adaptable, and genuinely curious who can use that tooling to go further, faster, and think proactively about how the process itself should keep improving.

What You'll Work On

FIX Onboarding & Integrations:

  • Lead and manage FIX client onboarding projects — from initial requirements gathering through certification and production go-live.

  • Configure, test, and validate FIX sessions, including order routing, execution reporting, and market data flows.

  • Coordinate conformance testing and certification with clients to ensure compliance with platform standards.

  • Document onboarding procedures, client configurations, and integration best practices.

  • Leverage internal AI and automation tools to streamline client onboarding and troubleshooting — including tooling built specifically for this function, giving you a genuine head start on deep process knowledge.

  • Collaborate with engineering and product teams to support new FIX workflows, APIs, and client integration initiatives.

Client Services:

  • Serve as frontline technical support for clients in EMEA across FX and equities business lines.

  • Build and maintain strong client relationships, ensuring timely and transparent communication addressing their needs and queries with professionalism and efficiency.

  • Provide ongoing technical and operational support for production trading environments.

  • Manage client inquiries, troubleshoot workflow or configuration issues, and coordinate resolutions across internal teams.

  • Partner with account management, sales and product teams to ensure a positive client experience and successful delivery of platform enhancements.

What We Need

  • 2-5 years of experience in a client onboarding, integration, or technical support role within financial technology, trading, or brokerage.

  • Good working knowledge of the FIX protocol — message structures, session management, and common trading workflows.

  • Genuine comfort troubleshooting FIX connectivity, analysing logs, and resolving integration issues, with the judgement to know when to dig deeper.

  • Familiarity with FX and Equities trading environments, order lifecycle management, and market data connectivity — genuine interest in working across multiple asset classes rather than staying within one.

  • A genuinely proactive, tech-first mindset — someone who treats our AI and automation tooling as a way to go further and faster, not a replacement for good judgement, and who naturally looks for ways to improve a process rather than simply following it.

  • Excellent communication and organisational skills, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple onboarding/client projects in parallel.

Nice-to-have:

  • Experience with OMS/EMS platforms, liquidity aggregators, or trading system integrations.

  • Exposure to other API protocols and architectures (REST, WebSocket) — relevant given the depth of our own API.

  • Scripting or automation experience (e.g. Python) and familiarity with monitoring tools (Splunk, Grafana, or similar).

  • Understanding of financial market structure and post-trade workflows.

What You Get

  • A genuinely rich API to work with — not a thin FIX wrapper bolted onto a legacy system. You'll onboard clients onto an API with real depth across order routing, execution reporting, and market data — the kind of platform where understanding the protocol properly actually matters.

  • Breadth across FX, Equities, and digital assets — most FIX/onboarding roles sit inside a single asset class. Here you'll build knowledge across all three, at a network connecting 40+ liquidity providers — exposure that compounds faster than a single-product environment.

  • Real ownership of the tech-to-business bridge — you're not just configuring sessions, you're the person translating FIX/API detail into client outcomes clients actually care about. That combination — technical credibility plus commercial judgement, is the actual shape of this role.

  • A genuinely tech-first operation — we've built dedicated AI tooling for this function specifically, so your ramp-up is faster and your day-to-day is spent on the client and integration problems that need real judgement, not repetitive configuration work.

  • A small, senior team — you'll work directly alongside Client Services, TechOps, and engineering, with real visibility into how the platform works end to end, not a large layer of process between you and the people who built it.

  • Growth across the business — the skills this role builds (protocol depth, client-facing technical credibility, cross-asset exposure) are the same ones that open doors internally.

  • Competitive package — up to 30 days leave + bank holidays, private health insurance, pension, life insurance, dental/optical cashback, cycle to work, socials and offsites

Our Hiring Process

We keep our process focused and respectful of your time. Our process follows three stages.

Stage 1: Initial Conversation with Talent Acquisition
Format: Video call, ~30-45 minutes

Stage 2: Team Conversation with one or two members of the Client Services team
Format: Video call or In-person, interactive session, ~60 minutes

Stage 3: Leadership Conversation with CRO

Format: Video call or In-person, ~60 minutes

What to expect in each stage will be explained by Talent Acquisition if you're invited to interview. Throughout the process, we aim to keep momentum with no unnecessary delays between stages, and feedback typically comes within a few business days.

*Please note that depending on availability, Stage 2 and 3 may swap around.

How to Apply

Please apply directly via this job posting — all applications, including those submitted via LinkedIn, are managed through our applicant tracking system, so you'll always land in the same place regardless of where you found this role.

Right to Work: Candidates must have the existing right to work in the UK. We are not currently able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Equal Opportunities: Reactive Markets is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation.

Reasonable Adjustments: If you need any adjustments or support during the application or interview process, please let us know — we're happy to accommodate.

Senior Frontend Engineer

Remote (UK-based) | Full-Time

About Us

Reactive Markets is the 2026 OTC Trading Platform of the Year (Risk.net). Our network handles over $75 billion in daily trading volumes across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency, connecting 50+ of the world's leading liquidity providers.

We build trading systems that operate at the edge of what's technically possible — where nanoseconds matter and a dropped message costs real money. Our engineering team is small, senior, and deeply invested in the craft of building cutting edge, reliable, high-performance systems.

The Role

We're looking for a senior full-stack engineer to build the trading platform our clients use every day. Despite the "frontend" name, this is not a UI-only role — our Frontend team works across the whole application stack in TypeScript and Rust, from the trader-facing interfaces down to the services behind them. It's distinct from our Backend team, who own the low-latency C++/Go trading engine.

This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who takes on the hardest problems and delivers them under their own steam. You'll own complex, ambiguous, performance-critical work end-to-end — designed, built, tested, deployed, and supported in production. You lead through code, craft, and mentoring, setting the technical example the rest of the team calibrates to. This is not a role where you write code and throw it over a wall: our engineers own the full lifecycle, and when something breaks, you're part of the team that investigates and fixes it.

Occasional hours outside the normal working day are required for production releases, scheduled maintenance windows, and Level 3 support during critical incidents. We keep this to a minimum and recognise the commitment — but owning a production trading platform means being there when it matters.

What You'll Work On

  • Complex full-stack features in TypeScript and Rust — from trader-facing interfaces to the application services behind them

  • Real-time market-data presentation and high-throughput, low-latency application code across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency

  • React and reactive state management (RX, MobX, or similar) for demanding, data-dense trading interfaces

  • Distributed systems and real-time data over REST, WebSockets, and network protocols

  • Architecture and solution design for the hardest technical problems the team faces

  • Observability and monitoring — dashboards, alerting, and metrics that make frontend behaviour visible

  • Production systems that handle real money — reliability is not optional

What We Need

Technical:

  • Strong full-stack engineering ability with deep TypeScript / JavaScript (ES6+) (5+ years)

Technical Delivery Analyst

Remote (UK-based)

About Us

Reactive Markets is the 2026 OTC Trading Platform of the Year (Risk.net). Our network handles over $50 billion in daily trading volumes across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency, connecting 40+ of the world's leading liquidity providers.

We build trading systems that operate at the edge of what's technically possible — where nanoseconds matter and a dropped message costs real money. Our engineering team is small, senior, and deeply invested in the craft of building cutting edge, reliable, high-performance systems.

The Role

We're hiring the first dedicated Technical Delivery Analyst. You will own the delivery of software projects end-to-end — from requirements through to production — working alongside engineers to ensure work lands on time, risks are visible, and stakeholders always know where things stand. As our engineering organisation grows into more specialised teams, you are the person who sits across the space between them — owning the dependencies, coordination, and communication that no single team owns.

This is not an administrative role. You need to understand the technology being built, speak credibly with engineers about architecture and trade-offs, and translate technical reality into clear communication for the business. You are the person who knows what is happening, why it matters, and what might go wrong — and you make sure everyone else knows too.

You will work closely with the Head of Technical Delivery and daily with Engineering, TechOps, and Product, with regular interaction with client-facing teams (Sales, Client Services). The role offers a clear path to Delivery Manager as the team grows and you take on broader ownership.

What You'll Work On

Delivery Ownership:

  • Own projects from inception to production — responsible for outcomes, not just process

  • Understand technical scope, architecture, and dependencies well enough to anticipate problems before they surface

  • Ensure infrastructure, testing, performance, and operational readiness are considered from the start

  • Know the current state of your projects at all times

Communication:

  • Communicate early and often — bad news delivered early is manageable; bad news delivered late is a crisis

  • Provide honest, accurate status updates — never spin, never hide, never assume someone else will raise it

  • Tailor to the audience — technical detail for engineers, business impact for leadership, actionable clarity for everyone

Technical Engagement:

  • Participate meaningfully in technical discussions — you don't write code, but you understand what is being built and why

  • Engage with engineers on architecture, dependencies, and integration points to accurately assess delivery risk

  • Bridge engineering and business by translating technical constraints into language stakeholders can act on

Risk Management:

  • Identify risks early through genuine understanding of the work, not by reading ticket statuses

  • Escalate with context — what is the risk, what is the impact, what are the options

  • Contribute to post-incident reviews with a delivery lens — impact, learnings, prevention

Continuous Improvement:

  • Look for friction in how work flows and propose practical improvements

  • Experiment with AI tooling to improve delivery efficiency — reporting, analysis, coordination, and communication

  • Maintain delivery tooling as a means to an end, not an end in itself

What We Need

Technical:

  • 2+ years' experience in technical delivery, project management, or software engineering

  • Previously worked as a software developer, or strong hands-on technical experience with software systems

  • Comfortable reading code, reviewing pull requests for context, and understanding technical trade-offs without simplification

  • Knows what "done" looks like in production — tested, deployed, monitored, documented

  • Familiarity with Agile practices and tools (Jira, Confluence) — values principles over ceremony

  • Financial services or trading technology experience is a strong advantage

How you work:

  • You own it. End-to-end responsibility. If it's your project, it's your problem — you don't wait for someone to tell you something is off

  • You communicate clearly. Exceptional written and verbal communication. Concise, precise, and honest under pressure. Confident raising difficult topics early — with engineers, stakeholders, and leadership alike — and you absorb pushback as readily as you give it, redirecting heat toward the outcome rather than taking it personally

  • You build trust. Engineers respect people who understand the work, tell the truth, and follow through — not a title. You are genuinely interested in the people you work with, and over time they bring you problems before those problems reach a ticket

  • You steady the room. When a project is drifting or an incident is live, you lower the temperature rather than raise it — calm, calibrated, and focused on what needs to happen next

  • You think in outcomes. Updating a board is not the same as delivering software. You impose structure where needed without over-engineering process

  • You stay technically curious. You genuinely want to understand how systems work and fit together. You don't simplify away the complexity that matters

  • You write things down. Documentation is how we scale knowledge across a distributed team. If it's not written down, it doesn't exist

  • You exercise judgement. You know when to escalate, when to solve, and when to ask for help

  • You embrace AI tooling. We use AI tools to amplify our delivery capability — from reporting and analysis to coordination and communication. You should be curious and willing to learn

What You Get

  • Real delivery problems — owning end-to-end project outcomes on a market-leading trading platform with genuine scale and technical depth

  • Breadth of exposure — work across the full engineering organisation: backend, frontend, platform, infrastructure, and TechOps

  • An excellent team — senior engineers who care about craft, collaborate openly, and hold each other to high standards

  • Direct mentorship — access to the Head of Technical Delivery for coaching, feedback, and professional development

  • Career progression — a clear path to Delivery Manager as the team grows and you take on broader ownership

  • Competitive package — up to 30 days leave + bank holidays, private health insurance, pension, life insurance, dental/optical cashback, cycle to work, socials and offsites

  • Remote-friendly — work from home with flexibility. We trust our people to deliver

  • Sustainable pace — we work hard, but we don't burn people out. Balance is how we stay sharp

We believe in transparency, honest feedback, and writing things down. We celebrate delivery, not activity. We frame AI as empowering people — removing toil, amplifying capability, enabling higher-value work.

We aim to build systems that don't depend on the heroics of individuals to maintain and support — systems and processes that are resilient, documented, and sustainable.

Our Hiring Process

We keep our process focused and respectful of your time. Our process follows three stages.

Stage 1: Initial Conversation with Talent Acquisition
Format: Video call, ~30-45 minutes

Stage 2: Hiring Manager Conversation with the relevant team lead or hiring manager
Format: Video call, ~60 minutes

Stage 3: Senior Leadership Conversation with our CTO

Format: Video call, ~60 minutes

What to expect in each stage will be explained by Talent Acquisition if you're invited to interview. Throughout the process, we aim to keep momentum with no unnecessary delays between stages, and feedback typically comes within a few business days.

*Please note that depending on availability, Stage 2 and 3 may swap around.

Please apply directly via this job posting — all applications, including those submitted via LinkedIn, are managed through our applicant tracking system, so you'll always land in the same place regardless of where you found this role.

Operations Engineer

Hybrid or Remote (UK-based), Hybrid or Remote (US-based) or In-Office (Singapore-based) Full-Time

About Us

Reactive Markets is the 2026 OTC Trading Platform of the Year (Risk.net). Our network handles over $75 billion in daily trading volumes across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency, connecting 50+ of the world's leading liquidity providers.

We build trading systems that operate at the edge of what's technically possible — where nanoseconds matter and a dropped message costs real money. Our engineering team is small, senior, and deeply invested in the craft of building cutting edge, reliable, high-performance systems.

The Role

As an Operations Engineer, you will ensure the stability, performance, and availability of the Reactive trading platform. This is a hands-on, technical operations role — focused on production systems, infrastructure, and trading workflows rather than client relationship management.

You'll work closely with Engineering, Product, and internal stakeholders as the first line of defence for live trading systems. TechOps owns Level 1 and Level 2 support — monitoring response and alert triage through to the deeper technical investigation, configuration delivery, and post-release verification that sits beneath it — escalating to Level 3 (Engineering and Infrastructure) only when an issue genuinely requires code changes or deep infrastructure intervention. While the role involves supporting client onboarding and integrations, the emphasis is on technical delivery, system correctness, and incident response — not sales or account management.

Reactive runs a globally distributed, follow-the-sun operations team, and we are hiring across our UK, US, and Singapore hubs. You'll provide operational coverage across your regional trading session — the eyes on the platform when your region is live — and hand over cleanly to the next hub as the day moves. In each region you own the full TechOps remit: monitoring and incident response through the session, plus the configuration delivery, onboarding execution, and change work that keeps the platform growing. The UK and US roles are remote; the Singapore role is office-based.

We are a small team that has turned operations into a genuine engineering discipline, and we are investing heavily in AI-assisted tooling and knowledge engineering to keep it that way. This role suits someone with experience in trading or FinTech operations who enjoys working close to production systems, solving complex problems, writing things down properly, and taking ownership in a fast-moving environment.

What You'll Work On

Production Monitoring & Incident Response:

  • Monitor live trading systems across multiple regions, venues, and asset classes — you are the eyes on the platform during the trading session

  • Own Level 1 and Level 2 response: triage alerts, run standard runbook actions (restart, rollback, failover, feature flag), investigate deeply, declare severity, and coordinate incidents — escalating to Level 3 (Engineering / Infrastructure) only when code or deep infrastructure intervention is genuinely required

  • Participate in failover and disaster-recovery readiness — rehearsed, playbook-driven, and time-bound

  • Drive root-cause analysis and blameless post-incident reviews, turning every incident into a runbook or a tooling improvement

Configuration Delivery & Production Change:

  • Deliver the production-change pipeline that brings new clients, liquidity providers, venues, and capabilities live — the largest share of the work

  • Configure and maintain FIX sessions by function — streaming, RFQ, algo, and post-trade — alongside cross-rates, indications of interest, subscriptions, certificate rotations, and pool registrations

  • Execute changes safely against the platform's deployment configuration, with schema updates, ACL coordination, and post-release verification

  • Support migrations, decommissioning, and the follow-on work that keeps the production estate coherent as it grows

Client Onboarding & Connectivity:

  • Own the technical execution of client and LP onboarding: credentials, IPs, conformance and UAT testing, cross-connects, day-1 readiness, and post-go-live verification

  • Act as the technical point of contact during onboarding, giving Client Services the information they need to manage the relationship

  • Monitor and validate FIX message flows, identifying issues related to execution, routing, or market-data

  • Maintain clear, accurate documentation for configurations, onboarding steps, and troubleshooting

Knowledge Engineering, Automation & Continuous Improvement:

  • Contribute to capacity and infrastructure planning — session load balancing, gateway placement, and utilisation monitoring — jointly with Performance Engineering and Infrastructure

  • Coordinate with external vendors and counterparties: network and colocation providers, post-trade vendors, and liquidity providers and their infrastructure teams

C++ Software Engineer

Remote (UK-based) | Full-Time

About Us

Reactive Markets is the 2026 OTC Trading Platform of the Year (Risk.net). Our network handles over $75 billion in daily trading volumes across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency, connecting 50+ of the world's leading liquidity providers.

We build trading systems that operate at the edge of what's technically possible — where nanoseconds matter and a dropped message costs real money. Our engineering team is small, senior, and deeply invested in the craft of building cutting edge, reliable, high-performance systems.

The Role

We're looking for a C++ Software Engineer who wants to build low-latency trading infrastructure on Linux. You'll work on the core components of our Switchboard trading platform — pricing engines, connectivity gateways, market-data systems, and the messaging layer that ties them together.

This is not a role where you write code and throw it over a wall. You build it, you test it, you deploy it, you support it in production, and you improve it. Our engineers own the full lifecycle — from design through to operational excellence. When something breaks at 4pm on a Friday, you're part of the team that investigates and fixes it.

Occasional hours outside the normal working day are required for production releases, scheduled maintenance windows, and Level 3 support during critical incidents. We keep this to a minimum and recognise the commitment — but owning a production trading platform means being there when it matters.

What You'll Work On

  • Modern C++20 and Go on Linux — a modern software stack based on open source

  • Cloud-native infrastructure on AWS with colocation in key data centres

  • Microsecond-level latency optimisation and high-throughput messaging

  • Market-data and reference-data pipelines across multiple asset classes

  • FIX protocol integrations with global banks and liquidity providers

  • Observability and monitoring — dashboards, alerting, and metrics that make system behaviour visible

  • Production systems that handle real money — reliability is not optional

What We Need

Technical:

  • Strong C++ with Linux systems programming (3+ years)

  • Comfortable working close to the metal — you understand what's underneath your code

  • Experience with performance-sensitive systems (profiling, optimisation, deterministic behaviour)

  • Familiarity with networking fundamentals (TCP/UDP, socket programming)

  • Go experience is a strong bonus — we use Go extensively for microservices and command-line tooling, and you'll be expected to work with it internally. If you don't know it yet, strong C++ engineers pick it up quickly

  • Python for scripting, automation, testing, and data analysis — used across the platform for tooling and operational workflows

  • Git and shell scripting

  • Experience in financial services or trading technology is a plus but not essential

How you work:

  • You ship. You're delivery-focused — you iterate, you improve, you get things into production

  • You own it. When you build something, you take responsibility for its behaviour in production. You respond to incidents (15-minute acknowledgement SLA during working hours), investigate issues, and close the loop

  • You write things down. Documentation is not an afterthought — it's how we scale knowledge across a distributed team. If it's not written down, it doesn't exist

  • You communicate. We're a distributed team across multiple time zones. Clear, proactive communication — especially when things go wrong — is essential

  • You care about quality. You write clean, testable code. You review your peers' work thoughtfully. You push for continuous improvement without gold-plating

  • You embrace AI tooling. We use AI tools (Claude, Gemini) to amplify our engineering capability — from code review and debugging to incident investigation and documentation. You don't need to be an expert, but you should be curious and willing to learn

What You Get

  • Real problems — trading systems where performance is measured in microseconds, not user clicks

  • An excellent team — senior engineers who care about craft, collaborate openly, and hold each other to high standards

  • Ownership — small teams, clear accountability, direct impact on the platform and our clients

  • Competitive package — up to 30 days leave + bank holidays, private health insurance, pension, life insurance, dental/optical cashback, cycle to work, socials and offsites

  • Remote-friendly — work from home with flexibility. We trust our people to deliver

  • Sustainable pace — we work hard, but we don't burn people out. Balance is how we stay sharp

  • Growth — career progression to senior roles, performance specialisation, or technical leadership. We invest in people who invest in us

We believe in transparency, honest feedback, and writing things down. We celebrate delivery, not activity. We frame AI as empowering people — removing toil, amplifying capability, enabling higher-value work.

We aim to build systems that don't depend on the heroics of individuals to maintain and support — systems and processes that are resilient, documented, and sustainable.

Our Hiring Process

We keep our process focused and respectful of your time. Our process follows three stages.

Stage 1: Initial Conversation with Talent Acquisition
Format: Video call, ~30-45 minutes

Stage 2: Hiring Manager Conversation with the relevant team lead or hiring manager
Format: Video call, ~60 minutes

Stage 3: Technical Interview with two members of the relevant engineering team
Format: Video call, interactive session, ~60 minutes

What to expect in each stage will be explained by Talent Acquisition if you're invited to interview. Throughout the process, we aim to keep momentum with no unnecessary delays between stages, and feedback typically comes within a few business days.

*Please note that depending on availability, Stage 2 and 3 may swap around.

Please apply directly via this job posting — all applications, including those submitted via LinkedIn, are managed through our applicant tracking system, so you'll always land in the same place regardless of where you found this role.

This is a hands-on role in a small, expert infrastructure team. You’ll work closely with our Head of Infrastructure, following problems from the cross-connect through hosts, containers and AWS. You’ll also help keep infrastructure delivery on track, from timelines and reporting to working closely with our TechOps team.

  • Low-latency networking across our colocation sites: switching and routing, cross-connects, BGP peering with liquidity providers and clients, and the fabric that carries our trading traffic

  • Bringing new sites to application-ready, starting with Tokyo

  • Our hybrid connectivity into multi-region AWS, including Direct Connect, routing and failover

  • Linux hosts and containers on the critical path, with every change made through code (Ansible, Git, Terraform), never by hand

  • Monitoring and alerting that catches problems before clients do, plus runbooks and post-incident reviews that someone else can follow

  • Planning and capacity: forecasting growth, setting timelines and reporting progress to TechOps and engineering

  • 4+ years running production infrastructure in a latency-sensitive environment, such as HFT, an exchange, market data or bank trading infrastructure

  • Colocation experience: cabinets, cross-connects, remote hands and vendor management

  • Solid Linux (RHEL) and TCP/IP, and the ability to trace a problem from the wire to the application

  • Infrastructure as code and containers as your default way of working

  • Working knowledge of AWS networking, and the confidence to pick up the rest of our stack. Networking depth matters more to us than any particular cloud or platform tooling

  • Methodical, evidence-led troubleshooting and clear documentation

A strong plus:

  • Project management experience: owning timelines, reporting progress, and working with ops teams to hit deadlines

  • Kernel bypass (Onload/ef_vi), PTP and time synchronisation

  • Experience bringing up a new colo site

  • FIX protocol or OTC FX market knowledge

  • Python for tooling

We’re a team with flexible hours, so time worked out of hours is taken back during the week. Day-to-day work is remote, with occasional visits to our data centres, most often in London (Slough).

What You Get

  • Real ownership of a live global trading network, hands-on, with few layers of process

  • A build-out year, with a new Tokyo data centre in Q1 and more growth ahead

  • A senior seat in a small, expert team where your changes ship and are measured

  • Competitive package — up to 38 days leave (inc. bank holidays), private health insurance, pension, life insurance, dental/optical cashback, cycle to work, socials and offsites

  • Remote-friendly working with flexibility around out-of-hours work

  • Growth as the estate scales
